## Q1
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R

Assertion (A): Higher cyclomatic complexity indicates a more complex program.<br>
Reason (R): It is calculated based on the number of independent execution paths in the program.

## Q1 - Options
(A) Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
(B) Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
(C) A is correct but R is not correct
(D) A is not correct but R is correct

## Q1 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** Software Testing, V&V & Quality (CMM)
**Source:** UGC NET Jan 2026 (2 Jan, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q21

Cyclomatic complexity is a direct measure of a program's structural complexity, so a higher value does indicate a more complex program, confirming Assertion A.

Reason R correctly explains why. Cyclomatic complexity is computed from the number of linearly independent paths through the program's control flow graph, and more independent paths mean more distinct execution routes to understand and test, which is exactly what makes a program more complex. Reason R therefore correctly explains Assertion A.

## Q2
Which of the following statements are correct regarding task elaboration in interface design?

A. Alpha testing is done at the developer's site in a controlled environment.<br>
B. Beta testing is done at the end-user site with developer presence.<br>
C. Acceptance testing may be very formal and last for weeks.<br>
D. Alpha testing always replaces Beta testing.

## Q2 - Options
(A) A, B, C Only
(B) A, B, D Only
(C) B, C, D only
(D) A, B, C, D

## Q2 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** Software Testing, V&V & Quality (CMM)
**Source:** UGC NET Jan 2026 (2 Jan, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q86

Alpha and Beta testing are distinguished by where they happen and whether the developer is present, and checking each statement against that standard software engineering picture is what resolves this item.

- **A. Alpha testing is done at the developer's site in a controlled environment.** — correct, Alpha testing is conducted at the developer's site with the developer able to control and monitor the environment.
- **B. Beta testing is done at the end-user site with developer presence.** — as worded, this is not correct. Beta testing is conducted at one or more end-user sites, but specifically without the developer present, in an environment the developer cannot control, which is what makes it a realistic field test.
- **C. Acceptance testing may be very formal and last for weeks.** — correct, acceptance testing can range from a few informal test cases to a planned, formal series of tests run over an extended period.
- **D. Alpha testing always replaces Beta testing.** — wrong, Alpha and Beta testing serve different purposes, and rigorous engineering practice normally conducts both rather than treating one as a substitute for the other.

Taken literally, only A and C are correct statements on their own, but among the given combinations, A, B, C Only is the closest match because it contains both genuinely correct statements and adds only one incorrect one, whereas the remaining options also misclassify D or drop a correct statement.

## Q11
A software system experienced five failures during testing. The time elapsed since the previous failure, in hours, is shown in the table.

| Error number | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Time since last failure (hours) | 6 | 4 | 8 | 5 | 6 |

Using the exponential reliability model with the failure rate estimated from the mean time between these five failures, what is the reliability of the software running for the next one hour without failing?

## Q11 - Options
(A) e^(−9/29)
(B) e^(−7/29)
(C) e^(−5/29)
(D) e^(−3/29)

## Q11 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Software Testing, V&V & Quality (CMM)
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2023 (17 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q3

The exponential software-reliability model estimates the failure rate as the number of observed failures divided by the total observed operating time, then applies R(t) = e^(-λt) for future operating time t.

Total elapsed time across the five recorded failures = 6 + 4 + 8 + 5 + 6 = 29 hours.

Failure rate λ = (number of failures observed) / (total time) = 5/29 per hour.

Reliability of no failure in the next hour, R(1) = e^(-λ×1) = e^(-5/29).

- **A. e^(−9/29)** — does not correspond to the ratio of failures to total observed time.
- **B. e^(−7/29)** — not obtainable from the given failure count or total time.
- **C. e^(−5/29)** — correct. It uses the correct failure rate of 5 failures over 29 hours.
- **D. e^(−3/29)** — understates the failure count used in the rate estimate.

## Q12
Consider the following statements:<br>
A. Dynamic metrics are collected by measurements made of a program in execution<br>
B. Static metrics are collected by measurements made of representations of the system<br>
C. The assessment of software quality is an objective process<br>
D. An important part of quality assurance in the selection of standards that should apply to the software development process.

## Q12 - Options
(A) A, B, C only
(B) B, C and D only
(C) A, C and D only
(D) A, B and D only

## Q12 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** Software Testing, V&V & Quality (CMM)
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2023 (17 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q49

Check each statement against standard software-metrics and quality-assurance definitions.

- **A.** True. Dynamic metrics come from measuring a running program, such as execution time or the number of errors observed during execution.
- **B.** True. Static metrics come from measurements of representations of the system, such as source code, design documents, or specifications, without running the program.
- **C.** False. Software quality is difficult to define precisely, and assessing it is widely recognized as a subjective process, since different stakeholders weigh attributes like usability, maintainability, and reliability differently.
- **D.** True. A key part of quality assurance is selecting the standards and procedures that will govern the software development process.

Only A, B, and D hold, so the correct combination is A, B and D only.

## Q13
\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ is intended to show that a system both conforms to its specifications and meets the expectations of the system customer.

## Q13 - Options
(A) Software specification
(B) Software design
(C) Software evaluation
(D) software validation

## Q13 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** Software Testing, V&V & Quality (CMM)
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2023 (17 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q53

Sommerville's software engineering framework distinguishes verification from validation: verification asks "are we building the product right" (conformance to specification), while validation asks "are we building the right product" (meeting the customer's real expectations). The definition given here combines both conditions explicitly — conforming to specification and meeting the customer's expectations — which is precisely the textbook definition of software validation.

- **A. Software specification** — the activity of writing down what the system should do, not the check that it was done correctly.
- **B. Software design** — the activity of planning the system's structure, unrelated to this checking activity.
- **C. Software evaluation** — not a standard named software engineering process activity.
- **D. software validation** — correct. It is defined as showing the system conforms to its specification and satisfies customer expectations.

## Q15
The cyclomatic complexity metric provides the designer with information regarding the number of \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_.

## Q15 - Options
(A) Cycles in the program
(B) Errors in the program
(C) Independent logic paths in the program
(D) Statements in the program

## Q15 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Software Testing, V&V & Quality (CMM)
**Source:** UGC NET Mar 2023 (15 Mar, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q24

Cyclomatic complexity is a structural software metric computed from a program's control flow graph, and it equals the number of linearly independent paths through that graph.

This count of independent logic paths tells a tester the minimum number of test cases needed to exercise every distinct path at least once, which is why it is used for test-coverage planning rather than for counting cycles, errors, or plain statement count directly.

## Q16

## Q17
Which of the following need not be assessed during unit testing?

A. Algorithmic performance<br>
B. Number of lines of code<br>
C. Error handling<br>
D. Execution paths

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

## Q17 - Options
(A) A, B, C only
(B) A, B, D only
(C) A, C, D only
(D) B, C, D only

## Q17 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** Software Testing, V&V & Quality (CMM)
**Source:** UGC NET Mar 2023 (15 Mar, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q54

The classic unit-testing checklist targets a module's interface, its local data structures, boundary conditions, its independent execution paths, and its error-handling paths, all correctness concerns internal to one module.

Raw algorithmic performance (runtime efficiency) is the concern of separate performance testing rather than a unit test's correctness check, and the number of lines of code is a size metric, not something a unit test verifies at all, so neither A nor B belongs to what unit testing assesses.

Error handling and execution paths, by contrast, are explicitly part of the standard unit-testing checklist, since a unit test specifically exercises a module's independent paths and its error-handling logic for correctness. Because some course materials draw this boundary differently, this item is worth checking against the specific textbook checklist used in the course.

## Q18
Match List I with List II.

| List-I | List-II |
|---|---|
| A. Condition coverage | I. Black box testing |
| B. Equivalence class Partitioning | II. System testing |
| C. Volume testing | III. White box testing |
| D. Alpha testing | IV. Performance testing |

## Q18 - Options
(A) A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I
(B) A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II
(C) A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III
(D) A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

## Q18 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** Software Testing, V&V & Quality (CMM)
**Source:** UGC NET Mar 2023 (15 Mar, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q70

Each testing term is matched to the broader testing category it belongs to.

Condition coverage examines a program's internal logic and branch conditions, which is a structural, white-box testing technique, giving A-III.

Equivalence class partitioning designs test cases purely from the specification without looking at internal code, which is the defining trait of black box testing, giving B-I.

Volume testing checks how a system behaves under large quantities of data, which is a form of performance testing, giving C-IV.

Alpha testing is conducted in-house on a nearly complete product to evaluate it as a whole before release, which aligns it with system-level testing, giving D-II.

This gives the mapping A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

## Q19
For a function of two variables, boundary value analysis yields,

## Q19 - Options
(A) 4n+3 test cases
(B) 4n+1 test cases
(C) n+4 test cases
(D) 2n+4 test cases

## Q19 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** Software Testing, V&V & Quality (CMM)
**Source:** UGC NET Mar 2023 (11 Mar, Shift 2) · Paper 2 · Q24

The standard boundary value analysis formula for a function of n variables is 4n+1 test cases, covering the minimum, just-above-minimum, nominal, just-below-maximum, and maximum values for each variable while holding the others at their nominal value.

For n=2 variables, this gives 4(2)+1 = 9 test cases.
